How to read this report

What do "broken through it" and "doubled slash" mean?

Sometimes page B is fine if you go there the right way, but page A links to it in a way that adds an extra slash, e.g. example.com/foo//page_B/ or example.com/foo/page_B//, or links to a URL that redirects to one like it.

If you navigate from A to B that way, page B will work, but all of its relative links (../../blah) are broken because of the extra slash in the path. They are not counted against page B, because there's nothing wrong there: the problem is in page A. So A's link is listed as broken, with the reason doubled_slash, and the links on B that the extra slash breaks, and those on every other page at a doubled URL that B's relative links lead on to, are counted on page A as "broken through it".

What is a "pedantic" link?

Humans generally write URLs like example.com/foo but technically the correct form is example.com/foo/: notice the trailing slash. These are actually two separate web pages as far as most web servers are concerned, and if you visit the first one the web server will helpfully tell your browser, "Hey dummy, there's no page here, it's over at example.com/foo/". So your browser has to make a second request.

Should the "wrong" URL count as broken, considering that the reader eventually ends up in the right place? It's debatable, but it is certainly lower priority than an actually broken link (a 404, say). These are not counted as broken: they are under Housekeeping's redirected links, marked as pedantic with a ring, after the other redirects.
